title: CAN IT OUTSHINE THE REDMI NOTE 4? (read full review to find out!)
author: Jeron
comments: Lenovo has been keeping a low profile when it comes to marketing its own smartphones. This in turn has lead many to assume that Lenovo will step back as the focus shifts back to Motorola. But it seems the Lenovo branded smartphones are not going anywhere. Rather than trying to do things differently, Lenovo seems more keen to strengthen its base and focus on core features; and the result is the K8 Note. Its new smartphone is a refined device, as it runs on stock version of Android; there are two cameras on the back as well.=============================Design: Metal body, offers good grip.=============================Lenovo K8 Note is a metal-clad smartphone with a matte black finish. The full metal body, flat side panels which slightly arch towards the back improve grip quality and comfort levels when you are holding it. It is 8.5mm thick but feels a bit hefty at 180g. Its closest rival, the Xiaomi Redmi Note 4, is also 8.5mm thick but lighter (165g). It is also splash resistant, which means you can use it when its raining.The regular physical attributes in K8 Note are all in the right places. The dual speakers are placed along with the micro USB slot at the base, so the sound won’t get muffled when you are holding the phone. The fingerprint sensor is placed at the back right under the dual camera module and can be easily accessed. It is also accurate and fast. The volume and power keys are placed side-by-side on the right spine. They are easily accessible as they are closer to middle, but feel a bit stiff when pressed. One unique addition the phone is the dedicate music key which serves as shortcut to music apps. Long press can play/pause music, double press switches track and pressing it thrice takes you back to the previous track.Overall, the K8 Note doesn’t really stand out from other smartphones in terms of looks. The Redmi Note 4 also has a metal body and back-facing fingerprint sensor, but lacks protection against water.------------------------------------------- Display: Big screen looks good-------------------------------------------The smartphone sticks to the usual 5.5-inch screen size and packs an impressive resolution of 1,920x1,080p, like the Redmi Note 4. It is a good looking screen which knows how to handle colours. Video playback and games look impressive, while text in ebook and webpages looks crisp. Visibility from wide angles is good and so is the legibility in bright light. Lenovo has added a colour mode which allows one to enhance colours while watching movies and switch back to a slightly dull look while reading. The Redmi Note 4 has a slightly brighter screen, but it is more prone to scratches than the K8 Note, which has Gorilla Glass 3.============================Software: In favour of plain Android============================Lenovo has turned a new leaf by switching to stock Android interface, like Moto smartphones, in the K series. It runs on Android 7.1.1. The biggest advantage of plain Android is less clutter and it shows in the K8 Note. There are hardly any third-party apps except a bunch of Microsoft apps such as Outlook, One Note, Skype and Excel. The Redmi Note 4 runs Android 7.0 but with a heavy and complex custom UI, called MIUI. It can be pretty annoying if you are more used to plain Android interfaces===================================Performance: Works smoothly and lasts long===================================The K8 Note is powered by MediaTek’s new MT6797 deca-core processor also known as Helio X23. It is a powerful processor and with 4GB RAM was able to run most tasks we threw at it with amazing grace. Even with multiple apps running in the background, games such as FIFA 16 and Big Bash 2016 played without any stutter. Unlike some of the earlier smartphones in the K series, there are no heating issues on this one. The Redmi Note 4, driven by Qualcomm Snapdragon 625 octa-core processor with 4GB RAM and 64GB storage, is quite powerful and at par with the K8 Note.The Lenovo smartphone offers 64GB storage and can take in microSD cards up to 256GB, which puts it at par with the Redmi Note 4. But unlike the Xiaomi smartphone which comes with a hybrid card tray, this one has a dedicated microSD card slot.When it comes to audio output, the K8 Note is a different beast altogether. Powered by Dolby Atmos technology, it delivers a loud and clear 360-degree sound effect in the headphone. It is an ideal smartphone for music buffs right now.With a 4,000mAh battery inside, the K8 Note can last longer than we expected. It can last a day and half of rigorous use and about 2 days on modest use, which is slightly better than the Redmi Note 4 which packs in a 4,100mAH battery.============================Camera: Impresses in all conditions============================The smartphone’s key attraction is the dual 13- and 5-megapixel camera set up to create better depth of field in images. The camera is fast and supports touch to focus. The picture quality in day light is impressive for a budget smartphone. Colours look accurate, while in landscape shots, the detail it can muster is way better than the Redmi Note 4’s single 13-megapixel camera. The Redmi Note 4 also tries to play with colours for more effect. Low light output is as blurry as the Xiaomi smartphone.The 13-megapxiel snapper on the front is backed by flash and can capture clear-looking shots even in indoor conditions.Specifications:-1.Operating System: Android 7.1 Nougat with Android UI2.Display: 5.5-inch Full HD display with Cornilla Gorilla Glass 33.Processor: 2.3 GHz Deca Core MediaTek Helio X23 (MT6797)4.RAM: 3GB RAM and 4GB RAM5.Internal Storage: 32GB and 64GB (Expandable upto 128GB)6.Camera: 13MP main camera + 5MP secondary camera for depth-sensing camera, 13MP front camera7.Battery: 4000mAh battery8.Dual Sim9.Splash ResistantIn the box:1.Lenovo K8 Note2.User Guide3.Sim Ejector tool4.Transparent Case5.Adapter6.USB CablePros:-)1.Android Nougat2.Solid build quality3.Dedicated slots for SIM and Micro SD cards4.Customizable Music Key5.TheaterMax VR support6.Cornilla Gorilla Glass Protection7.Smooth Performance8.Turbo Charging9.Dolby Atmos for Better 3D song10.LED Flash for Front CameraCons:-(1.Poor Low Light Camera Performance2.Non-Removable Battery3.Little Heavy4.Dual Camera needs Improvement5.Gets warm Quickly6.Does not have 4K video Recording========  Verdict========Lenovo has got most things right with the K8 Note. The dual camera, big screen, plain Android and steady performance are some of the elements which are hard to find under the same roof. The Redmi Note 4 is one of the best smartphones at this price point but the complex UI, average camera and scratch prone display, hybrid card slot are some of the features which Lenovo has taken care of in the K8 Note.So that's it guys if you like my review Kindly mark the " Helpful" option below so this may be useful to others too....&.You owe me a Smile :-)

comments: I've been using the phone (4GB variant) from the past 1 month and I must say.. it's a bang for the buck.  The pros and the cons have been listed below:Pros:1. The front 13MP camera with flash makes those perfect selfie shots actually possible that I always wanted to take.3. title: Good value for money; disappointing dual-camera
author: Amazon Customer
comments: I would have happily given a 4* rating had it not been for the atrocious delivery quality of Amazon.Positives:- It has a premium look and feel, and good build quality.- Setting up was easy.- Battery life is quite good, with more than 1 day for my normal usage.- Display quality is very good.- Both front and rear cameras are reasonably good for the average user.  Read negatives below.- Split screen feature with two apps running at the same time is useful for people who really need it.  Otherwise a novelty.- Flash can be turned on in video recording, which is another novelty with no significant improvement in video brightness except a drain on the battery.Negatives:- Lenovo claims turbo-charging, but with the standard micro-USB port and the charger provided, charging is not very fast.  It took about 90 minutes to charge from 15% to full.  Would hardly qualify as 'turbo'.- The Nougat OS provided is stock android with very little customisation possibilities, so may not be liked by users who are used to heavy UIs on other phones - but once you get used to it you will start accepting it.- The bokeh effect with dual rear camera is just so-so, and many times the layer separation is not as precise as you expect it to be, so you will not get desired results everytime. Also, when you turn on the dual camera, the front layer is also slightly out of focus.  On the whole, you can forget that you have dual rear cameras, and stick to single camera mode for peace of mind.- Missing 'slow-motion' and 4K recording are a shame.  Panorama mode does not even cover 180 degrees.Overall good value for money.  Go for it if you want performance and not care for camera features.

title: So far so good...
author: Aditya
comments: I upgraded from K3 Note to this device, not because I like Lenovo but because they experiment with new hardware to give best 'on paper' specs in a given price tag. This phone too comes with a brand new processor in the market and Lenovo's first dual-lens setup. Did they do a great job?Well, the phone is fast, but not lightening fast (cannot be compared to a Samsung S8) but its fast enough to multitask, game and stuff. The processor heats up on maximum load (as expected from Mediatek), but the temperature doesn't go above 43° which is a step up (my K3 Note used to cross 50°). And the chip isn't power efficient (not as much as a snapdragon processor), so the battery lasts longer on a Redmi Note 4 though they both have same capacity (i.e., 4000 mAh).The camera is an experiment too, so depth effect isn't very good, the focus takes very long and the camera application has a lot of important features missing (that the Moto has).The stock Android is good. Its smooth and bloatware free. But its too bare, the hardware can do so much better, there would be custom roms soon out there that would show the full potential of the hardware, but we gotta wait for now. For a normal user ( not an advance user), the stock Android is the right thing, so don't judge on this basis, this is my personal opinion.The plus points of this phone are way more than the minus points, I don't have words for them. Overall its an awesome device, I am satisfied.

The speaker could've been louder but overall does a good job. Dolby Atmos feature works as expected and the music experience is great on this phone especially over  headphones. Combine Dolby Atmos with Lenovo's Theatre max feature with a VR Headset and watching movies over this phone is simply amazing.The all metal build quality is good but the phone does feel a bit heavy and the shape of the phone doesn't help alleviate the issue. Would've preferred a front finger print sensor but that's just a personal preference. Battery would last a day or longer depending on usage and the included fast charger works as advertised. title: A worthy descendant of 3T!
author: Anoop C
comments: Am a die hard One Plus fan, having bought my One Plus One way back when the brand first came to India. It stayed with me for 2.5 years of trouble free existence and got a great resale price too. I later got a One Plus 3T and now for last two days has been using One plus 5T. It does not disappoint and has the same built quality and premium feel of it's illustrious predecessors. 6 inch screen in awesome, so seems the improved camera and it's features, from my limited use in these few days. Battery life is same as most other smartphones with similar screen size, dash charge works like a charm.Comparing with 3T or even 5, one major problem (at least for me) is the placement of the virtual home button. To increase screen size, the physical home button has been moved, with the fingerprint scanner now in the back. Though it is seamlessly done and scanner in back works well, typing has become an issue, for me. The spacebar, while typing is now just below the home button. So every now and then, unless one is really careful, the home button is mistakenly pressed while typing. Can be quite irritating - hope One Plus will look into it. Otherwise, an absolute value for money flagship phone, one that you can own with pride.

title: Best in its class and in the class above.
author: Ameya Godbole
comments: Well.. It's the best bang-for-the-buck cellphone available today. Period. Don't let anyone tell you otherwise, and don't worry about after-sales service either. I've bought this after using a Oneplus 2 for two years straight and I can vouch for their service. Plus the build quality is such that you are only required to take basic care of the phone. It's not a delicate dolly like the iPhone or all the Samsung phones.Pros:1. OLED display was a great move by Oneplus. Colours are poppy and the blacks are really black and makes the dark theme my favorite.2. Dash charge - You've got to use it to believe it. It puts all other fast chargers to shame. No wireless charging? No problem. I've got dash charge bruh.3. Portrait mode - the depth effect (bokeh) works fantastically well. The colour reproduction is natural and the dynamic range is wide enough to capture most of the shades in nature. It's not in the league of Pixel 2XL or the iPhone X, but hey.. Look what you're paying for it.4.Battery life - I wasn't expecting much from it but it has succeeded in surprising me! I am yet to end a day without at least 25% battery left. I am a heavy user, mind you. In terms of SOT (Screen On Time), I have consistently gotten 7+ hours. 8.5 if I stick on WiFi the whole day. I cannot ask for more.5. Sheer speed - Snapdragon 835 and near stock android is the perfect recipe. No lag whatsoever! Trust me, you get so addicted to the speed after a while that every other phone seems slower. I'm not kidding. Even Note 8 seemed slower. It probably is.Cons:1. No portrait mode on the front camera - I'm not much of a selfie person but this might be a con for a lot of people.2. No feature for NFC payment - it has NFC but no built-in feature to use it for NFC based payments like Samsung Pay. I'd appreciate if Oneplus launches a standalone app for this. Otherwise there's not much use for the NFC.3. No OIS (Optical image stabilization) - the cameras are great no doubt. OIS would have made the phone a little more expensive and I guess Oneplus decided that it was an acceptable tradeoff. The absense of OIS isn't going to hamper pictures taken in usual situations, but you'll miss it while taking adventure shots or while taking pictures or shooting videos while moving.These cons are just a case of me nitpicking. This is definitely the best phone to buy under 40k. If that's your budget range then just stop thinking and get it.

title: Far from 'Perfect'
author: Elton XS
comments: In-Depth ReviewLet's get straight to it: The BIGGEST SETBACK in this device is the absence of Optical Image Stabilization.This absolutely sucks and is apparent when doing a video recording.Still images are impressive - but not always (again, Image Stabilization could come in handy if you have shaky hands)The 16MP rear camera offers stunning portrait photography.  However, the camera doesn't perform very well at night.USB media transfer wasn't straight forward and is surprisingly time consuming. I expected it to be as simple as  connecting the phone to your computer, but it's not. You've set it to Media Transfer (under developer settings) to get it to work. :/Fall test: Survived a minor fall purchase. (It had the cover on though.) I hear the bare aluminum body can be easily dented so be careful.Always ready to go: Dash Charge is amazing. It makes operating the OP5T a seamless, fluid and uninterrupted experience. It's charges incredible fast!Storage: 64 GB simply would not do it for me. I have a ton of music, tv shows, and movies that I transfer back and forth. Not to mention the large Image size when captured in highest resolution.Since, the OP5T does not offer expandable memory, you simply need the 128 GB model.Users should note that you get only 111 GB of usable memory.The Screen is a delight to look it. It offers vibrant colours and deep blacks. No complains here. The face unlock works really well but I find myself using the fingerprint scanner more often.The 2:1 aspect ratio is fun to look at but can be annoying while texting - the bezel less display means the home/back buttons are now on screen RIGHT UNDER the keyboard 'spacebar'. I've been "accidentally sent back to the home screen" more times than I'd like to admit :|Apart from that I greatly appreciate Oneplus' Oxygen UI - it's awesome! I love that this phone has a schedule power on/off feature to automatically turn your device off at nights to save battery life in the long run.Processing is super smooth. With the 6GB/8GB RAM can run any app out there.However, I was disappointed that the phone did heat up during gaming (with multiple apps running in the background)The OP5T is slim, sleek, light weight and easy to carry. It's a beautiful device and a joy to use - but at this price point the absence of Optical Image stabilization is a setback I simply cannot ignore.4/5.

title: The Honest OnePlus 5T review.
author: Illusion
comments: First of all, I would like to mention my current usage scenario with existing phones and with Oneplus 5T phone.I have Samsung Galaxy S7 Edge 32 gb and iPhone 8 plus 256 gb.I've been a big fan of Samsung flagships and I've used Samsung Note, Note 2, Note 3, Note 4 and now S7 edge. There is no doubt about the fact that there is no competitor of Samsung in the market when it comes to Android phone with the best features.I've been using s7 edge for last one and half years and it is really awesome. The only reason I didn't go for Samsung Galaxy note 8 or Galaxy S8 was because of slow performance of Samsung phones due to bloats that you could not uninstall even if you don't need them.I've finally switched to OP5T and this is my experience so far.PROS:1. The phone is packed with the best hardware in the market so it is too powerful and damn faster than S7 edge.2. FaceID and Fingerprint censors are too fast compared to S7edge.3. FaceID works good even in low light situation.4. Battery life is really good for a heavy user like me. I always have Bluetooth ON with at least one device connected, WiFi and mobile data always ON and at least 6 hours on phone calls every day. In this scenario, the battery drains to 10% from 9AM to 8PM that is damn good backup. (S7 failed to do that).5. Screen resolution is good enough and impressive. You would definitely enjoy watching movies, playing games etc.6. Dash charging is insanely fast as they claim it to be. 50% battery charged in less than 20 minutes charging time.7. Data transfer through USB-C is fast enough for me.8. Camera is good for an average use. (Not for hardcore photographers).9. Phone doesn't get heated up like crazy as it used to in previous models even in charging or heavy usage case.10. No freakin bloats like Samsung and other brands that is a big relief for me.11. Speaker and audio quality is good though the speaker volume is a bit lower than other flagships in the market like S7 edge.CONS:1. Playing games will drain out the batter like crazy so be careful you have a power source with you especially when you are outa office or home.2. Camera quality is good but not great compared to S7Edge. Samsung still beats OP5T camera so that is an area of improvement. Low light camera could use lots of improvements.3. FaceID recognition doesn't work sometimes in low light case and doesn't work ever in the dark (Can't expect iPhone X accuracy and precision at this price  lol).4. Call drop issues sometimes even with full carrier signal though the problem is rare.5. Screen resolution is lagging behind the latest competition but it is still good enough.6. It is not waterproof/water resistant that is like a common feature in flagships from other brands though I'm good without it.Overall it is a nice phone to have with latest hardware and good switch over for other flagship phones users like me.

title: Review after 1 month of usage : Near flagship, Bang for your buck. Puts the competitors in same price bracket to eternal shame.
author: Aswin K.
comments: Used the phone for about a month now.. Loving it. Worth every penny.Pros:1. Super fast&light OOS paired with snap dragon 835 SoC. Tasks and switching between apps in this device works without any hick ups.  Flagship smart phone experience for half of the price.Oreo update available.2. Plenty of RAM to keep multitasking works like a charm. Got the 8 GB variant,seems like an overkill but it makes it kind of future proof for next 2 years at least.3. Excellent battery life considering the capacity is only 3300 mAh. Usually gets around a day with 7-8 hrs of SOT and lasts for 1.5 days with moderate usage with 4G/WiFi on always. Use it with greenify app to get the max out of your battery and enabling doze mode in developer options.4. Dash charging - a blessing from one plus. Fastest in the World.Charges the battery from 10 % to 100 with in an hour. Just charge it for around 30 min , you will have enough juice for the day.5. Great AMOLED display with deep blacks and a bit saturated colors. Watching HD videos in this is a treat for your eyes.Believe me you don't need QHD display crammed in to a 6" size, our eyes cant tell the difference between 1080p and QHD with this pixel density. Also keeping a darker theme can make the UI look absolutely stunning and helps with the battery too.6. Great camera performance. Portrait mode works good and gives okayish bokeh effect for social media pics. Low light performance is also good with both the cameras. Pro mode in camera is a pretty nice feature if you are familiar with DSLR and can shoot in RAW  :) .7. Light and Slim build.8. Blazing fast face unlock and fingerprint unlock.Cons:1. Not much cons I have experienced , sometimes the in call volume feels to be on the lesser side compared to my previous phone.2. Though the phone looks premium, it feels very slippery in hand.Use of a case is very much recommended. Oneplus could have made a sandstone version :( .NB: You don't have to compare this with other mobiles in similar price range like Samsung A8+. This beauty performs better than my friends S8+ in day to day tasks for half the price.

title: Value for Money
author: Babu Natarajan
comments: Ordered on Prime's Nov 21 sale, and got it on the same day. There are many Pros and few Cons. Tested it on various conditions. Listing them below.Pros :Fast ChargingProcessorNever run out of memoryNo lag in gamingPortrait modeSleek designQuick face unlock (even works in low light with 50% display brightness)Easy accessible Fingerprint sensor (lightning speed)Gestures using fingerprintOxygen OS 4.7Loud SpeakerSingle hand usageDND slider is hard (it slider easily in OP5, and was a big problem)Cons :5t doesn't support Project Treble (Mobiles launching with Oreo should opt for Treble, that's another reason why OP5t came with Nougat)Pathetic Lowlight camera performance (full of noise)Gets heat (only when running huge multiprocess)Display could be betterMobile vibrates when music plays in full volumeOreo not onboardedLess detailed SelfiesAfter 5 days of usage, can say that Battery backup is too good and almost last a day as of now, but I fear it won't after 6 months of usage if your an extensive user. Even with 200+ apps installed and 20+ running in background, it provides me run for a day. 90 mins of FullHD video play took 12% charge (11% in S8+) which is good in this range. 0 to 100% battery reaches in around 40-45 mins.Oneplus commented that it placed secondary rear camera sensor IMX376K a new one from Sony is determined for Lowlight photos. But it doesn't, and not understanding when aperture is what they want is tobe same why they opted for another sensor with 20 MP. Anyway portrait is getting better results than OP5, but Pixel2 and Pixel2 XL are clear winner in this range. And could have been better if Oneplus given Note8 like future to increase and decrease blur strength. Sometimes edges are not well defined in portraits. Photos are mostly warm and washed. Front camera's selfies not producing details, actually all it does is beautify. More like any Chinese selfie oriented camera.Display is ok in this range but could definitely be better when it was 2960*1440. But nevertheless backed by a good AMOLED display.Missing Stereo speakers, boarded speaker is too loud and it vibrates playing music in full volume. When low-end mobiles also offers dual, Dolby Atmos and stereo (in premium mobiles) missing them in this killer. Audiophiles would feel bad for its effect in headphones, may work well with Bullet V2.To those who expect, wireless charging I don't believe in it, it requires a glass back which will make the mobile fragile and cost you high when up for replacement. And Dash charger is 20W powered, wireless is yet to get such a lightning fast technology.Missing Oreo and it's features is a major drawback.Now a days we are getting compromises even during the launch of Flagship is what reminding, let's take Pixel2 and Pixel2 XL launched with loads of bugs and Apple is also not out of this, we see many are balming IOS11 and iPhone 8 and iPhone 8+ isnt selling as expected are the clear proof. There were times where companies provided features for customers, but now you need to compromise for a period and live with bugs. Meanwhile your warranty would be tampered and no longer the company need to think about you. The same behavior attracting the OnePlus.Anyway, OnePlus is definitely a best upgrade and OnePlus will laud about it for sometime.

title: The TRUE "Flagship Killer" of 2017
author: Nikhil
comments: Now that I have my hands on this beautiful phone, I'm so glad to have resisted the urge to get the Oneplus 5! ^_^This is by far the best > value for money flagship < of the year!Here's some honest feedback about this Beast from the time I've spent with it:1) Design:Finally, Oneplus has caught up with other companies and introduced a new bezel-less design which is just magnificent! The fingerprint scanner at the back is lightning quick and the all-metal body feels super premium with its trademark svelte soft touch feel.There's no advertised dust and water resistance but at this price, it is a little too much to ask from the company, in my opinion.2) Display:The new 18:9 AMOLED display is a delight to look at. One of the best displays to use, even under direct sunlight! Accurate colors and lots and lots and lots of screen!!3) Battery life:The Oneplus 5T should easily last more than a day for an average smartphone user. For the geeks, it should give you around 5-7 hours of Screen-On Time. Dash charge is probably the BEST charging solution ever introduced in the market. You can charge your phone from 0 to 100% in just 60 MINUTES!!! It is just INSANE!!4) Software:The 5T runs Android 7.1.1 Nougat with an Oxygen OS overlay on top of it. Overall it is a well-rounded mix of pure android with some essential add-ons. Screen-Off gestures are one of my personal favorites! With 8GB RAM, you will never be left wanting more from your phone!!5) Sound:The single bottom firing loudspeaker is pretty darn loud on this phone. The highs and lows are clearly distinguishable, and the overall sound is much richer than on the Oneplus 5!6) Camera:Oneplus swapped the zoom camera on the OP5 with another low-light camera on the OP5T and personally, I am very happy with that decision! I would rather be able to capture beautiful night scenes than be able to optically zoom in without losing quality. Portrait mode is another defining feature of this device! Compared to the OP5, the portraits are much better in all aspects, with a better separation between the subject and background!All in all, if you are on the lookout for a phone that doesn't burn a hole in you pocket but still manages to challenge the Galaxy S8/S8+, Iphone X or the Google Pixels, I've got just one thing to say to you:BUY THIS PHONE NOW!!!click on the yes button if this helped you make the right choice! ^_^

title: The best smartphone of 2017.
author: Amazon Customer
comments: The best phone I've used this year, hands down.Improves upon the flaws of it's predecessor. Gorgeous display. Very capable camera. Lightning fast.Beautiful minimalistic design. Looks even better with the official OnePlus Karbon bumper case, slapped on.Top of the line processor, stock Android with useful tweaks, paired with 8 GB of RAM makes this device lighting fast.No transitional animations at all. title: Outstanding phone with amazing performance
author: Akhil
comments: This is the cheapest phone with latest snapdragon 835 octa core processor with 8GB of ram. This is a performance beast and can handle many apps and graphics intensive games (used asphalt8, shadow fight 3 and many others) easily. No lag of any kind at all and very responsive.The screen is so immersive that you wont like to put phone down. Many apps and games already support HD+ screen and it is an amazing experience. The face lock is very quick but I wont rely too much on that and would prefer using finger-print lock.I am using two sims (jio and vodafone) and use 4g all the time. I have moderate usage and even after 24 hours of last charge I am still left with around 60 pct of battery, so amazing battery life.The camera takes crisp pictures and cannot complain at all about it. I have not tested its low-light capabilities so cannot comment on that. The device is so sleek that I sometimes even forget that I am carrying my phone in my pocket. I was using one plus two earlier and its remarkable improvement over that phone. They also provide a clear back cover along with pre-applied screen protector which is a plus. I am fan of flip cover though as IMO they look more professional and provide better protection. So still waiting for a good one to come.The dash charger is so damn fast that in half an hour you will get battery juice for at least 8 hours. The oxygen OS is also very smooth to use.So to summarize: gorgeous screen, sleek metal body, awesome camera, amazing battery life, dual sim, powerful hardware in an android phone. What else can anybody ask for?

title: Worth a buy
author: Hrishikesh kasture
comments: Well to start with, I was looking for a compact, branded, Bluetooth speaker with a long lasting battery.Expected use: While travelling & for soft listening at home - especially at night in my bedroom.Did some reading before opting for this one ... especially all the reviews that were posted here.Must say that some of the reviews were quite informative & helpful for my decision making process. Hence this review to help others like me.Let me start with the packingAmazon packing was not as per expectations ... just average. The item was in a bubble wrap which was surrounded by a plastic bag. Ideally I expected a hard card brown box .... if you know what I meanThe original JBL packing was quite good, with protection in the form of a plastic enclosure with some cushion due to the way the packing was designed. If it wouldn’t have been for this original packing, the speaker could have been damaged with the kind of packing provided by Amazon.At the bottom of the box you’ll find booklets on warranty information, safety instructions, a guide & a usb cable. I was expecting a keychain to a part of the package ...  was also expecting a pouch which is absent here.The size of the speaker is extremely compact ... fits in my palm perfectly.It seems to be a little heavy (not in a bad way) considering its size .. which means that there are quality components used.The speaker’s mat & rubbery finish add to the quality feel.JBL is mentioned at both front & back sides.It has a place where you can attach a key chain ...Five buttons on the top ... power, Bluetooth, volume + & -, call receive.Apart from these there is an aux input, usb charging port & mic.This speaker has excellent output & clarity considering its size ... I already had one guest taking a pic of it when I was playing it at home.The sound is very unidirectional especially the treble ... it’ll sound great if it’s facing you else you’ll tend to miss some of the effects if you are not in the front.Treble & mids are very good ... bass is average. You anyways can’t expect much from a speaker of this size with a marathon battery.The battery seems to be quite a workhorse. I’ve used this atleast for 3 hrs (couple of sessions) since it’s delivered & am yet to charge it for the 1st time.Choose pop / shocking colours cos they will look the best on this speaker.I’ve got a blue since that was the only option available in a lightening deal at Rs. 1600 in the great Indian sale.All in all, it’s worth a buy if you are looking for compact, Bluetooth speaker with a long lasting battery.If you find the review helpful, pls hit the like button.

title: Sony SRS XB-10 Bluetooth speakers- Compact yet powerful!
author: Salim Khan
comments: Hey guys this is Salim and since a long time I have been searching for good and cheap Bluetooth speakers and damn there were too many to choose from. As soon as I made my mind to buy, lets say speaker A, another one came to mind, and then another one and so on.I literally saw more than 100 speaker reviews. Some say these are good and some say that one is best.---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------On to the ReviewFinally I saw the Sony SRS XB-10 which was unreleased at the time of my purchase. There were good reviews for it on Amazon US. So I got it. I got this at a price of 3390 INR. I got two of them (more on that later)Looking at the speaker, its compact and is kind of a cylinder but not a cylinder. It has a mono speaker at top and a passive radiator for bass at the bottom. It has a cool SONY branding on the side of the speaker along with a few buttons :1. The Power button- for turning on the speakers as well as put it in pairing mode if long pressed (A led light is there also above the power button which blink slowly when turned on, stays lit when paired and blinks rapidly when in pairing mode).2. Volume buttons to adjust the volume according to your preference3. A Play Pause button which is a multi function button as it can be used to trigger OK Google or Siri and can also be used to take or end calls (Yes you can take calls with this- I dont know why you'll do that).4. An Add button- Basically if you have another XB10, you can use Add and either make the music go louder or have stereo sound i.e. left and right channels on separate speakers.5. It has a flap to the back which when opened reveals the micro-USB charging port as well as a 3.5mm audio jack(in case you want to listen using wires).Now Sony Claims a battery life up to 16 hours and I'm satisfied as I listened to music at 50% and its more than 16 hours ( 16 hours 20 mins to be technical) and there is still charge left in the speaker.Speaking of battery, the charge time claimed by SONY is 4:30 hours and it took me 4:20 to fully charge it.It has a led light for charging which turns red when charging and turns off when fully charged.It is IPX5 certified that means its water resistant to water splashes and a bit of dirt. You can use it in poolside parties (I dont know why you will do that as they are small and even though they are loud but not that loud) and also you can use it when showing in the bathroom (which I do a lot).It has NFC for one touch pairing and it works flawlessly with my Nexus 5X. I don't know why my OP3 had trouble pairing with it over NFC because the speaker works with all other NFC capable phones (I tested it).It has a cute little silicone strap to the back which is very useful in the shower for hanging purposes and this strap can also be used to place the speaker.The range of the speaker stated by SONY is 33 feet and that the norm these days in Bluetooth speakers.Coming to the main part: SOUNDThis is a speaker in the XB or Extra bass range which means the bass produced should be good and it is. When you listen to EDM's or Dance music or any music which has a lot of beats, the bass is damn good and its deep and punchy. I never thought speakers so small can produce such good bass.Now lets come to Treble.The audio is very clear. The voices are not muffled. Plus the voice/music does not break at full volume.That does not mean other genres like Rock sound bad. Its just that they don't sound as good as EDM'sOne more best part of it is the Add feature (which I mentioned earlier), when using 2 speakers and listening to EDM, it's damn pleasurable.So let's divide this into PROS and CONS,PROS:---------1. Deep and punchy bass. Amazing audio quality overall2. Very loud considering its size3. Price (Value for Money)4. IPX5 certified5. Has NFC(keeping in mind its price as well as brand name)6. Great Battery LifeCONS:----------1. Audio sometimes breaks in the starting of the first song.2. This is a con only for me. It doesn't pair well with my OP3 using NFC although other phones with NFC like Nexus 5X works well,This is not a CON but the colour stated as RED is actually ORANGE..You must be thinking I gave 2 cons, why am I giving it 5 Stars? Well to be honest I do not have the option to give it 4.9 stars :PSo should you buy this? Hell YESSure this doesn't have the fancy features like dual speakers or charging your mobile via the speaker (not to point out brands but JBL :P)Also keeping in mind its price and its brand name i.e. SONY, you should go for it (I know I said it earlier but I mean it now)And SONY is a huge and trusted brand in terms of audio ( only Audio :P)One thing that would make the product even more awesome. A way to know the battery left on it.So ya this is my full in depth review of the Sony SRS XB-10.Hope you guys got a correct understanding of the product.And if you didn't get it the first two times,  GO BUY ITYou can check out my channel for video reviews of other products on YT.Update: The charge lasted for 20 hours 31 min when volume is set to 50%. its way more than what Sony claims.Update 2: When connecting one speaker and using streaming apps like Netflix there is no audio sync issue but when we use dual speaker i.e. pair one more speaker, the audio goes out of sync by 0.5 sec (which is hardly noticeable, but once you notice it, it makes you crazy).Update 3: I found one more con, the inbuilt microphone on this speaker is pretty poor (atleast for my OP3). So giving it 4 stars now.

title: Great, durable little speaker!
author: Nihir Shah
comments: I am quite satisfied with this product. I have had it for several months and it does a great job! It has fallen and been moved around while renovating a house and it still works well. It may not be the best sound quality that your money can buy, but it sounds just fine to me. Best sound quality is turning your phone's volume to max and then adjusting the volume on the speaker. I wanted the most bang for my buck and I believe I found it with this speaker. I like the colors, the ease of use, sound quality, durability, and battery life. It is handy to be able to hang the speaker. I've used it for music and phone calls with the blue tooth connection. The range of the blue tooth is decent. I could have my phone in the living room and this speaker on the front stoop while I was painting outside. If it is paired to more than one device, it will switch over to the closest device. Thankfully, my son and I have relatively similar music taste. I recommend this product.

title: This speaker packs a punch!!

comments: This is the mid range speaker we all are looking at. Earlier i had ordered the Logitech x100 but the sound quality was not that great. So had to return back and did some thorough research for all speakers in the same range. Specially the JBL Go and the MI speaker and have to say the x50 stands tall. It is loud, has clean output with decent base. The battery life is great. It does not have calling feature which i feel is really not required. Overall this is a great offering from Logitech which nicely stacks up as a great home speaker!

title: Very good for the price range and compared to other Bluetooth speakers.
author: JAY KRISHNAKUMAR
comments: Quite good for the price. I bought this because my phone had awful speakers, I went with the reviews on YouTube and several forums and decided to order this. At first I was confused between X50 and X100 because they were so similarly priced but then decided to go with the X50 as I had no need for a microphone. Best decision I made. title: an unbias detailed review
author: srajak
comments: it is a great product there are many pros as compared to cons they are----✔✔✔✔✔PROS:✔✔✔✔✔✔ The speaker has a good Bluetooth range, it works up to 10 m. It supports almost all Bluetooth devices whether new or old. The speaker supports A2DP, AVRCP as well as HFP Bluetooth profile, so you can be sure that this will support your device as most of the device supports either of these profiles. To be more simple, it works between Bluetooth 2.1 to 4.0 and almost 99% devices are in this range of Bluetooth.✔ The speaker comes with a 3.5 mm audio-in port, so you can directly connect it to your phones, laptops, PCs or any electronic devices using a 3.5 mm aux cable which is also widely supported audio jack format nowadays. (AUX cable not included in package)✔ This speaker really gives a surround sound experience to the listener. It houses a 3.81 cm or 1.5 inch driver and a built-in amplifier. Philips have manufactured these speakers with an Anti-Clipping feature which prevents distortion in sound without affecting the loudness. This means that the amplifier wont let the speakers to clip i.e go beyond its maximum capability thus preventing any distortion even at high volume. So this I think is a very good feature to have in your speaker, because nobody wants poor sound on high volumes.✔ The speaker has a jaw-dropping clarity with a well balanced treble and a boom bass which makes it a must buy even at 1999 bucks. The speaker has good highs and lows and it gives a dynamic surround sound bass as well. So it is like a icing on the cake.✔ The Size!!! Now what can I say about that. This speaker easily slips into your pocket due to its super compact size. All you need to do is get your phone connected to the speaker and keep it in your pocket to enjoy songs on the go, its as simple as that. Philips seems to have created a compact boombox at this price.✔ Battery, now this is an important thing when it comes to Bluetooth speaker. The speaker comes with one Li-Po battery with 2 W power output. So the speaker works on very low energy yet produces gigantic bass and treble. All you need to do is charge it for 2 hours through either USB 1.1/2.0/3.0 or if your charging through an AC adapter then around 1 hour 15 minutes. When you start charging the white starts flashing and when it gets completed no LED is shown. Once charged this beast unleashes for 6 hours of playback time.✔ The Philips BT-50 is made of good quality plastic, or even may be carbon fibre, and over it, it has rubber coating throughout the whole body even the stand in the base has a rubber coating so that it does not slip off any slippery surface. It looks are really awesome and stylish. Believe me, no one can imagine that a speaker of this size can produce such high standard sound until they listen to it.✔ There is pairing switch to connect your device with the speaker if the connection does not occur automatically.✘✘✘✘✘CONS:✘✘✘✘✘✘ The speaker can't connect to more than one device at a time. But that is acceptable cause you can't listen to two devices simultaneously. But it could have been great if two could be connected at a time and one could be played as soon as the other is stopped.✘ The pack does not come with an aux cable or adapter, but only an USB cable, so you have to purchase an aux cable separately if you want to connect your device directly to the speaker.✘ No volume control option or play pause button. Though speakers comes with an internal amplifier but that works automatically to prevent clipping, no manual volume control is available.✘ The Philips branding on the body has started to scrape off (you can see in my posted pics). So keep it carefully and away from abrasion as much as possible.◘◘◘◘◘◘◘◘VERDICT:◘◘◘◘◘◘◘◘The speaker is really a good deal. Philips has yet again proved their intelligence in sheer sound quality by getting all the pieces at the right place. The speaker has good connection, simple setup and awesome sound, overall makes it a must buy. Though there are few cons but those are very much acceptable to the pros you get. The price is a bit high but this speaker deserves it and compared to other top brands like JBL for example, you get this speaker at a steal of a deal. Go for it. title: NICE DESIGN AND CHEAP
author: KartiK
comments: There are many compact portable speakers out in the market now. Among the big piles of these compact, tiny, ultra-portable, and any other terms you can call to these portable speakers, there are those that still offer affordable and quality ones.An example among them is the Philips BT50B-37 Wireless Portable Bluetooth Speaker. This compact portable speaker by Philips is very affordable and meets with the demands of every audiophile for an audio device that delivers quality sound and design.At a price of $19.99 only, you can now have the Philips BT50B-37 Wireless Portable Bluetooth Speaker. And what more can you ask for? It features impressive sound quality, quirky design, easy Bluetooth pairing option, and built-in microphone for speakerphone capability!Philips BT50B37 WirelessTo know more about the Philips BT50B-37 Wireless Portable Bluetooth Speaker, read our full review below.Philips BT50B37 WirelessPhilips BT50B/37 Wireless Portable Bluetooth Speaker – PerformanceAt its very compact size, who wouldn’t be surprised with how the Philips BT50B-37 Wireless Portable Bluetooth Speaker delivers an impressive sound quality?The Philips BT50B-37 Wireless Portable Bluetooth Speaker packs a single channel speaker that delivers a very clear and crisp sound. We were surprised to hear this sound quality for a portable speaker that is very compact and small. Aside from that, the sound we heard from this Philips speaker is absolutely full and detailed, thus having no distortions at all even if used at a higher level of volume.As what Philips is marketing with the Philips BT50B-37 Wireless Portable Bluetooth Speaker, this portable speaker has an anti-clipping function that lets it perform with high quality, especially keeping it from damage by distortion. Well, we prove this function to be very effective. The mids and highs were met with positive feedback, as well as the treble was delivered in high quality.Although if you are one who loves playing tracks that demands strong bass, well we suggest for you to consider other portable speakers. This is because we observed that the Philips BT50B-37 Wireless Portable Bluetooth Speaker has minimal to no bass output. For some compact, tiny, or ultra-portable speakers, this is expected, and so is with the Philips BT50B-37 Wireless Portable Bluetooth Speaker.When it comes to battery life, we observed this portable Bluetooth speaker to perform for up to 8 hours. This 8-hour battery life is already good for a tiny portable speaker like the Philips BT50B-37 Wireless Portable Bluetooth Speaker. This portable speaker comes with a standard micro-USB cable for you to recharge it.Philips BT50B37 WirelessPhilips BT50B/37 Wireless Portable Bluetooth Speaker – DesignThe Philips BT50B-37 Wireless Portable Bluetooth Speaker has got a beautiful and quirky design. We love how this portable Bluetooth speaker looks and maybe it is because of its shape and color combinations.The Philips BT50B-37 Wireless Portable Bluetooth Speaker is very compact, measuring a dimension of 3.0 x 2.4 x 2.4 inches, and very lightweight at 3 ounces only. This is one of the most compact portable speakers we have reviewed among Sony SRS-BTV5 Portable NFC Bluetooth Wireless Speaker, AYL Portable Speakers, and iHome IM60GT 3.5mm Aux Portable Speaker. It fits firmly in our palms and can easily be placed inside our backpacks and tote bags. Its enclosure is made with rubberized plastic that makes it really easy to grip. This really helps in avoiding slips and drops, thus reducing damage to this portable speaker.At the top of the Philips BT50B-37 Wireless Portable Bluetooth Speaker is where the speaker grille covering the single channel speaker is found. On its sides is where the Philips logo, LED light indicator, slider switch for Power Off/Aux Connection/Bluetooth Pairing, Phone button, and ports for micro-USB charging and Audio input are placed. While on its bottom part is a rubberized stopper to avoid the speaker to move while being used.The Philips BT50B-37 Wireless Portable Bluetooth Speaker is available in Black and two other quirky colors such as Gray/White and Lime/Gray.Philips BT50B37 WirelessPhilips BT50B/37 Wireless Portable Bluetooth Speaker – ConnectivityFor the connectivity options, the Philips BT50B-37 Wireless Portable Bluetooth Speaker supports Bluetooth connectivity and wired connectivity.Using the Bluetooth connectivity was very easy at all. The pairing process was fast as you only need to slide the switch to Bluetooth pairing mode, search the audio device in your smartphone or other gadget’s Bluetooth setting, then pair. If you prefer using wired connections, then the Philips BT50B-37 Wireless Portable Bluetooth Speaker has an input for 3.5mm Audio/Aux cable for use.Lastly, which we are very impressed too for this compact portable speaker to have is a built-in microphone for speakerphone capability. Aside from that, we found the speakerphone function to be at a decent quality based on our testing.THAT is IT GUYSi also like to do reviews on my youtube channel

title: BEST IN THIS RANGE// VERY STURDY // POWERFUL & GOOD QUALITY SOUND OUTPUT
author: Abraham JOSEPH
comments: I got this Bluetooth speakers a couple of days ago.I also own the boat rugby bluetooth speaker which are still running fine even after months of usage.So as far as the quality of boat products is concerned ,I am really satisfied with it.I can surely say the ,they make good quality products at really affordable price tag.Watch my latest video of TOP 5 affordable bluetooth speakers here youtu.be/nJhDpDs1o-c .It's in Hinglish :)﻿ Or you can visit my channel "NickCyber Reviews"Features:1-It is equipped with two front firing speakers(5w+5W= 10W POWER) with 40mm driver and a passive radiator for surround bass effect.2-It consists of a 1500mah Li-ion battery which will provide a battery backup of 8+ hours.3-IP-66 waterproof certification4-Shockproof design5-Inbuilt microphone6-AUX input supported#Build Quality--------------------- It's got 5 buttons on the longer side for power, volume+/-, play/pause, and Bluetooth reconnect. On one of the smaller sides (left of the speaker), theres a charging port, red led that indicates it's still charging, and an aux port that worked fine without any crazy static or cutting out. There's also a glaring blue light that shows in the speaker side (it's off center), and it will blink if it's searching for a device.-Water proofing?Everything is water resistant, as it's encased in a rubber body, and has a metal mesh covering the speakers.The boAt stone 600 is developed for outdoor and indoor activities, this can endure through heavy splashing or rain, sending water at all angles through a 12.5mm nozzle at a rate of 100 liters/min at a pressure of 100kN/m2 for 3 minutes from a distance of 3 meters. It complies with the stringent IPX6 Certification for 100% protection against water. The boAt Stone 600 shuts and blocks water splash, rain, dust or other type of moisture that would otherwise damage your speaker.#SOUND OUTPUT?--------------------------The sound is pretty is clear, and the bass is punchy.The boat rugby was not that good with bass.But this one really nailed it.For the price and size ,this is surely the most powerful one this range. You could put this in any corner of the room and hear it just fine.You can get this nice and loud, or really quiet too.There is minimum amount of distortion at higher volume levels.I found it better than my mini JBL Go.Anyway GO is far more portable.#Bluetooth Connection-------------------------------It comes with bluetooth 4.0 . As stated by the manufacturer ,Bluetooth 4.0 connects through using of three main protocols: Classic Bluetooth, Bluetooth High Speed and Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE). So now you can connect your Stone 600 with any Bluetooth device. With the newer low energy technology,Bluetooth 4.0 allows specify the re-connection timeout intervals for their devices, so devices can remain connected indefinitely without much of an effect on battery life.With CSR8635 you can stream High quality audios, iOS battery status monitor fully configurable EQ (5-band / 6-banks). Dynamic volume boost / cut. It also enables users to take HD Voice calls and charges the device much faster.I recommend this for anyone who just wants to have great sound around them. Of course not for throwing huge parties, but if its a small get together, this will work great.Range is decent when using Bluetooth from my Laptop (about 10 feet) but when using my cell phone (Oneplus X and iPhone 5) the Bluetooth range increased to about 20 feet with out drop out.The finish on the Boat Stone 600 is good and it looks pretty slick. While holding it, you can feel that it is good quality.Thanks for reading.I hope my review provided all the information for a well informed and wise purchase decision.I hope it helps :)-Abraham

title: Unbiased Review! - Really worth it??
author: SPK
comments: I've been using these speaker for more than 2 months and here's my review. [Unbiased]So,first thing first....Talking about the build quality I like it but I'm not so happy with the rubberize material used all over the body of the speaker except the front.The material is too attracted to dust.It's a dust magnet.I think this makes the speaker shock-proof but they should've used any another material.So, built quality - 3.9Now,the box contents....There's not so much in the box as expected but they should provide a gold-plated aux but instead they provided a ordinary aux cable.Coming to the sound quality......I'm really impressed with the quality of sound it reproduces.The clarity is so good and the sound is overall balanced and the amount of bass it produce is really good.But the bass comes to the personal preference.The sound should've been louder but it does the work in most situation.So,I ended up rating the sound quality - 4.4Now,let's talk about the battery life.......Here,I'm totally blown out with the battery backup this speaker can give.The company claims 8 hrs but with fully charged and keeping the volume  70-75% this bad boy gave me about 9-10 hrs of playback.The speaker takes little bit of long time to fully charge but once it is charged you are ready to GO....So,a big thumbs up to the battery life and I'll give the Battery - 4.6Time to talk about Shock and Water proof feature which is totally a life saver.......I dropped it nearly 10 times and it is working perfect and I'm sure that this guy will easily survive quite harsh drops.I took it to the shower and even tested by dipping under water and as expected it just survived like a boss.But an important thing to remember is that the rubber cap plays a vital role keeping water away from getting inside so always put the rubber cap very tightly and it will handle all the splashes and dips very easily.So,rating the Extra Features - 4.6SO, THE OVERALL RATING - 4.4That's all I have to say about this product.This BT Speaker is highly recommended.Give my review a thumb's up if you found it helpful.THANK YOU!

title: Excellent product, great sound for the price.
author: Sarat Chandra Gnanamgari
comments: I don't generally leave a written review because I think it's way too much work, but ever so often I come across a product so good that I'm shaken out of my torpor. I'd never been a fan of bluetooth speakers until I used a friend's Divoom Bluetune Bean and I was pleasantly surprised with the amount of volume it put out. Since then, I got myself on a relentless quest to find a good bluetooth speaker for under Rs. 2000. I went for the Logitech X100 first, but it just wasn't enough and there were connectivity issues very early on. The JBL Go worked fine but I needed something with a little more amplitude and I settled on the Soundbot after extensive research; the reviews on Amazon.com are very glowing. First thing you notice is the packaging which looks premium AF. Unpacking this was exciting, small touches, right? It has a 3.5mm cable, which I think is *very* thoughtful and useful. Other than that, you have your speaker, a USB cable and a booklet. Right out of the box, I tested the speaker and at its loudest, in a small room, I had to shout to make myself heard. This thing gets loud, no doubt about it. When possible you don't want it at its loudest though, although the distortion isn't extremely apparent, you'll immediately realize the value in topping the volume off at about 70-80%. The bass is well present and it puts out a balanced sound. Unchanged, the treble is a little more accentuated but I found that this could easily be corrected by using a good player. The battery life is phenomenal for a speaker which costs this much. On Bluetooth I got about 8.5 hours as opposed to the 10 hours advertised and this was fine. Using the 3.5mm cable, I got 12.5 hours, these tests were not controlled for level of volume, so the results might not be reliable, but I was extremely happy in either case. To sum it up, at what it costs, this is the best speaker you can buy, the higher you go, the better speaker you'll get, but if you just want a budget portable speaker which will put out good (and loud) sound, go for this, no questions asked.

title: Great product........
author: Chandrotpal
comments: I am writing this review after using it for a month. I must say the more time you spend with this product you are bound to like it, in fact you will fall in love with this speaker. Even now I am using Max Pi water proof/Bluetooth portable speaker which is an another excellent product with a lesser price. So I will just provide you a comparison between SoundBot SB571 & Max Pi C5 Bluetooth speaker:Looks: Both the speakers looks good.  SoundBot SB571 however looks more premium, on the other hand Max Pi due to much smaller in size and light weight is more portable and you can easily carry wherever you want!Durability: Both the product of great quality, but due to additional features like splash proof, dust proof you can use Maxi Pi outdoors whereas SoundBot SB571 intend to be more of a indoor speaker.Sound quality: Once again both the speakers equally good. But due to size and additional inbuilt speakers, SoundBot SB571 produces slightly better sound including bit superior BASS.Loudness: SoundBot SB571 is a clearly a winner in this department, it's too loud and you will be hardly using the full volume unless you use it outdoors.Sound clarity: I find SoundBot SB571 again bit better than Max Pi, but again max Pi is a wonder for it's size.Battery backup: SoundBot SB571 gives around 8 to 10 hours depending on the uses, but Max Pi is a clear winner here. Max Pi just goes on and on and you will tend to forget completely when last time you had charged it!!Verdict: If you are looking for a portable great quality speaker for both outdoor & indoor uses with features like shock/dust or water proof then Max Pi is your answer. But if you are looking for mainly an indoor speaker with excellent sound quality then go for SoundBot SB571.

author: Amazon Customer
comments: Initially, I was reluctant while ordering this speaker even though most of the customers gave a positive review about it. This is because it is an unknown brand. However, when I listened to it, I was amazed by the quality of sound it produces. The sound is crisp and very clear with negligible distortion at full volume. In fact, you can rarely listen to it at full volume as it becomes unbearably loud. My mother sitting far away from me could not bear it at full volume.Many people have told that it doesn't produces a very impressive bass. Let me tell that they cannot expect theater-like bass from such a small speaker. They should appreciate that the base it produces can be felt through the vibration it creates on the surface on which it is placed. I have listened to JBL as well but it doesn't produces as deep and immersive sound as this one.Since, I have received this product today, I cannot comment on its each and every aspect. But, so far I am totally satisfied by the sound quality that it offers at such a cheap price.I recommend it to anyone who is looking for a great speaker at a relatively low price.
